chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad — he elevated it (mursal) to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said:

'It was said to him: "What is the matter that the companions of Isa (peace be upon him) used to walk upon the water, and that is not found among the companions of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family)?" He said: "The companions of Isa (peace be upon him) were spared the concerns of livelihood, while these ones were tried with livelihood."'

key_terms.ابْتُلُوا: Were tried/tested; subjected to the trial of livelihood
key_terms.الْمَعَاش: Livelihood, means of living; the worldly concerns of earning and sustaining oneself
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: He raised it (mursal); a hadith chain with a gap, traced back without explicit connection
key_terms.كُفُوا: Were spared, sufficed, provided for; freed from the burden of earning

ai.seo_question: Why could the disciples of Jesus walk on water but not the companions of Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains why the companions of Prophet Isa (Jesus) were given the miracle of walking on water while the companions of Prophet Muhammad were not — namely that the former were provided for and freed from worldly concerns, whereas the latter were tested through the burden of earning a livelihood. This hadith reflects a profound theological point: spiritual capacity is not measured by miraculous powers, but by one's steadfastness under trials. The companions of Muhammad faced a more demanding test — navigating the demands of worldly life while remaining devoted to God.
